The design is settled, and three choices are left before I build. Settled tonight: George is the default voice, briefings live in the task folder, the plan skill stays as a small separate skill, and decisions are named in words, never numbered. The three things waiting on you are the code check, the build order, and the first project. I will take them one at a time.
Decision · Code check

Should the build step catch invented codes?

WarnRecommended

The build step lists anything that looks like a made-up label, a few letters and a number, so the agent rewrites it in plain words before you see it.

No check

Rely on the written rule alone, as the old kit did.

If you say nothing: Warn.

The first decision needs no background. Agents keep inventing labels, a few letters and a number, and expecting you to remember them. A written rule alone never stopped that. So, should the build step catch them? With the option called warn, the script that builds a briefing lists anything that looks like a made-up label, and the agent rewrites it in plain words before you ever see it. With no check, we rely on the written rule, as before. I recommend warn. If you say nothing, I go with warn.
Decision · Build order

What do I build first?

Presenting firstRecommended

The player, the build script and the presenting skill. Everything built after that can be reported to you as a briefing.

All at once

Guide, memory, plan, presenting, installer and migration in one pass. One big hand-off at the end.

If you say nothing: Presenting first.

The second decision is the build order. One option is presenting first: the player, the build script and the presenting skill. Then everything I build afterwards can be reported to you as a briefing. The other option is all at once: the guide, memory, plan, presenting, the installer and migration in a single pass, with one large hand-off at the end. I recommend presenting first. If you say nothing, I go with that.

Before the last decision: two places to try the kit

The talk repository

Small, already has its own work area in the old format, nothing else depends on its paths.

Productivity

The one you use every day. Hush lives inside the folder that would be renamed, so the rename has to wait until Hush moves out.

The last decision needs a little background. There are two natural places to try the new kit. One is the repository for your qualifying exam talk. It is small, it already has a work area in the old format, and nothing else depends on its paths. The other is Productivity itself, the one you use every day. There, Hush lives inside the folder that would be renamed, so the rename has to wait until Hush moves out.
Decision · First project

Where do I migrate first?

Talk repository firstRecommended

A full migration on something small. Mistakes are cheap, and it tests every step including the rename.

Productivity first

You get the benefit where you work, but the rename is deferred and Hush is in the way.

If you say nothing: Talk repository first.

So, where do I migrate first? Starting with the talk repository gives a full migration on something small, where mistakes are cheap, and it exercises every step including the rename. Starting with Productivity gives you the benefit where you actually work, but the rename is deferred and Hush is in the way. I recommend the talk repository first. If you say nothing, that is what I do.
